minutes.headline: Planning Board endorsed an ANR, approved two Conservation parking site plans and a Pleasant Street addition, and continued 494 Electric Ave to March 10.
minutes.summary: The board endorsed an ANR for 589 Flat Hill Road and approved a site plan for 110 Pleasant Street, then held hearings on three Conservation Commission and contractor site plans. The 494 Electric Avenue hearing took most of the night. The board split on the Pierce Avenue entrance and crosswalk, and the legal status of Pierce Avenue is still with Town Counsel. The board declined to sign two stormwater decisions over unclear wording, signed the common driveway decision, and discussed committee reports and its schedule.

attendees.role: town staff (planning staff, reads notices, minutes)
presenter (engineer for Conservation Commission and Paradis Contractors)

public_comment.topic: Mr McDonald (by Zoom) supported helping the Il Forno business succeed, asked whether the owner's preferred entrance was known, and suggested conditions to re-evaluate when the land across the street is developed.

Bob Pierce (11 Wintergreen Court) urged the board to take straw polls of members on difficult applications. He said the 494 Electric Ave project should have applied as a shopping center, and he objected to the withdrawal request.
A resident of 914 Northfield Road asked where the parking would go and whether it was near Stage Coach Road; she was told it is a separate hearing.
Bob Pierce described the planned loop trails and the connection to Parks and Rec land and Table Rock, in support of the 801 Northfield Road lot.
Michelle Matthew asked about parking near her property and Stage Coach Road, and was told the lot is about 200 feet away with access off Northfield Road.
Owner of Settlers Crossing Golf Course raised concerns about golf balls hitting cars, trespass onto the course, wetlands and runoff, and policing of the new lot.
Bob Pierce responded on behalf of the Conservation Commission: the lot avoids Stage Coach Road, and a similar lot on Holman Street has had few problems.
Michelle Matthew asked how people would reach the other parking area (801 Northfield Road).
Bob Pierce said he saw no golf balls and has flagged the trail route up to Table Rock.
Bob Pierce asked the board to again assign its MRPC GIS hours to the Conservation Commission for trail mapping.

votes.motion: Endorse the ANR for 589 Flat Hill Road.
Continue the 494 Electric Avenue site plan and stormwater permit hearing to March 10 at 6:05 p.m.
Close the public hearing for 801 Northfield Road.
Approve the site plan for 801 Northfield Road with standard conditions.
Continue the 994 Northfield Road public hearing to March 10 at 6:05 p.m.
Close the public hearing for 110 Pleasant Street.
Approve the site plan for 110 Pleasant Street with standard conditions.
Authorize the land use director to assign the MRPC GIS contribution to the Conservation Commission for trail mapping.
Approve the minutes of the February 10, 2025 meeting.

budget_items.topic: Town Counsel legal review of Pierce Avenue status (494 Electric Ave)
budget_items.what_was_said: Town Counsel is to give a cost estimate for the deep-dive legal review, which the applicant would pay, likely into escrow like a peer review. The estimate was not yet available.
A board member said they hoped the fee was waived and another thought it was; the applicant's representative thanked the board.

budget_items.topic: Conservation Commission grants for parking areas
budget_items.what_was_said: The engineer said grants funded both Conservation parking projects.

budget_items.topic: GIS mapping hours vs paid mapping
budget_items.what_was_said: Conservation would otherwise pay an hourly rate for map work; the board's eight free MRPC GIS hours go to them instead.

budget_items.topic: Municipal Building project at town meeting
budget_items.what_was_said: A member commented on the large cost of the building project and the effort to present it at town meeting.

decisions.decision: For 494 Electric Ave, the board will leave the Pierce Avenue entrance as designed for now and wait for Town Counsel's review of the road status; the applicant will return March 10.
The applicant will take the canopy to the land use director as a possible de minimis change to the prior approval, to be considered at the next meeting.
The March 10 meeting will go ahead despite overlapping the Citizens Caucus. Applicants are advised against scheduling special permits that night because of quorum risk.
The board did not sign the 255 Sunny Hill Road and 560 Goodrich Street stormwater decisions because the deed-recording wording and a special condition were unclear.
The board agreed to sign the common driveway decision for 558/560 Goodrich Street.
Community notices from neighboring towns will be emailed to the board as they arrive rather than read at meetings.
The Master Plan Steering Committee will keep its two vacant seats for now; the chair will ask the Select Board whether it wants to fill its seat.
The Open Space Committee review of the 100 Townsend Harbor Road property will go on the next agenda so the board can vote on a recommendation to the Select Board.
Review of standard operating procedures is deferred until the land use director is present.
The two zoning workshops were deferred because there was no guest and no land use director.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued the 494 Electric Avenue site plan and stormwater hearing to March 10, waiting on Town Counsel's review of Pierce Avenue's legal status.
The board endorsed an ANR for 589 Flat Hill Road by voice vote, with no opposition heard.
The board approved site plans, with standard conditions, for 801 Northfield Road (Conservation parking) and 110 Pleasant Street (shop addition).
The 994 Northfield Road Table Rock parking hearing was continued to March 10 after neighbor and golf course concerns.
The board declined to sign two stormwater decisions over unclear wording, and agreed to sign the 558/560 Goodrich Street common driveway decision.

why_it_matters: The Pierce Avenue question on Electric Avenue is unresolved, and Town Counsel's legal review would be paid for by the applicant, so the entrance design and the project's timing depend on it.
Two Conservation Commission trail parking lots on Northfield Road were before the board, one approved and one still open, and neighbors raised concerns about the second.
watch_next: March 10, 6:05 p.m.: the 494 Electric Avenue and 994 Northfield Road hearings resume, at a meeting that overlaps the Citizens Caucus and carries a quorum risk.
A Town Counsel cost estimate for the Pierce Avenue review, and an Open Space Committee recommendation on 100 Townsend Harbor Road, are due on a coming agenda.
